answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to wander through a sequence of costly peer challenges that leave permanent marble-like marks on a shared shale ledger of history. Only continuous%2C non-transferable proof of work across epochs allows an agent to accumulate standing%2C so an attacker must fund many parallel independent histories rather than cloning one cheaply. This raises the real resource cost of mass fake identities because each must independently wander and carve its own durable trail.
